recipe.title: Beef and Spinach Peanut Stew
recipe.description: A hearty Central African-inspired stew where tender beef meets fresh spinach in a rich peanut‑tomato broth, perfect for a filling midday meal.
instructions: Dice the beef into 2‑cm cubes.
Finely chop the onion and crush the garlic cloves.
In a large pot, heat a splash of oil over medium heat; add the onion and garlic, sauté 4 minutes until translucent.
Add the beef cubes, brown them on all sides, about 5 minutes; the juices should start to caramelize.
Stir in 100 g of raw peanuts; using a mortar or a food processor, blend the peanuts with a little water to form a smooth paste, then add the paste to the pot.
Pour in 600 ml of water, bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer (low heat).
Cook the stew for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beef is fork‑tender and the sauce has thickened (it should coat the back of a spoon).
Add the spinach, stir, and cook 3 minutes until wilted but still bright green.
Check the internal temperature of the beef with a thermometer; it must reach 63 °C and rest 3 minutes – the meat will be fully cooked and safe.
Season with a pinch of salt and pepper, give a final stir, and serve hot.
tips: If the sauce is too thick, add a little more water; if too thin, let it simmer uncovered for a few minutes.
For extra depth, add a small spoonful of tomato paste (optional, not from pantry).
Serve with boiled rice or boiled plantains for a complete meal.

recipe.title: Baked Plantain‑Spinach Casserole with Peanut Crust
recipe.description: A layered bake where sweet plantains and savory spinach are topped with a crunchy peanut crust, echoing the flavors of Central African home cooking.
instructions: Pre‑heat the oven to 190 °C.
Peel the plantains and slice them diagonally into ½‑cm thick rounds.

Arrange the slices on a baking sheet, brush lightly with oil, and bake 12 minutes on each side over medium heat until the edges are golden and the plantain is tender when pierced with a knife; set aside.
Roughly chop the onion and mince the garlic.
In a skillet over medium heat, sauté the onion and garlic for 4 minutes until fragrant and the onion becomes translucent.
Add the spinach, stir, and cook 3 minutes until wilted; season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
In a food processor, blend the raw peanuts with 150 ml of water until a coarse paste forms.
In a greased 20‑cm baking dish, layer half the plantain rounds, spread the spinach mixture, and repeat with the remaining plantains.
Spread the peanut paste evenly over the top, smoothing with the back of a spoon.
Bake the casserole for 20 minutes over medium heat until the peanut crust is set and lightly browned.
Remove from the oven, let rest 5 minutes, then slice and serve.
tips: If the plantains are very ripe, reduce baking time to avoid over‑softening.
For extra crunch, toast the peanuts lightly before blending.
A drizzle of a simple hot pepper oil (optional) adds a traditional kick.

recipe.description: A light yet nourishing soup that blends silky spinach and peanut broth, finished with crispy beef croutons—ideal for a quick lunch.

recipe.description: Capas de col crujiente y una masa ligera de harina, horneadas hasta dorar, una opción sencilla y sin grasa para la cena.

recipe.title: Spiced Cauliflower and Chickpea Curry
recipe.description: A hearty vegan curry featuring urgent cauliflower and protein‑rich chickpeas, flavored with garam masala and fresh tomatoes.
instructions: Rinse the 200 g dried chickpeas, place them in a bowl, cover with water and soak for at least 6 hours (or overnight).

Dice the onion, mince the 3 garlic cloves, and chop the tomatoes.

Stir in the cauliflower florets and sauté for 4 minutes, until they start to turn golden.
Add the chopped tomatoes, 2 tsp garam masala, and a pinch of salt; cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes break down.
Add the cooked chickpeas, mix well, and pour in 150 ml additional water if needed. Cover and simmer on low heat for 10 minutes, until the cauliflower is tender and the flavors meld.
Taste and adjust salt if necessary. Serve hot with rice or flatbread.
tips: If you have leftover cooked chickpeas, you can skip the soaking step and use them directly.

Remove the potatoes from the oven, let them rest for 2 minutes, then serve with the fresh tomato chutney.

recipe.description: A comforting oven‑baked casserole that layers fluffy rice with sweet corn and tender chicken, flavored with yellow chili paste and lime.

recipe.title: Risotto de calabacín y gambas
recipe.description: Un risotto cremoso con calabacines rallados y gambas jugosas, perfumado con ajo y limón.
instructions: Ralla los 2 calabacines y reserva.
Pela y pica finamente los 2 dientes de ajo.
En una olla grande, calienta 2 cda de aceite de oliva a fuego medio.
Añade el ajo y sofríe 1 minuto, hasta que esté dorado pero sin quemarse.
Incorpora el arroz arborio (200 g) y revuelve 2 minutos, hasta que los granos estén translúcidos.
Vierte 200 ml de caldo de verduras y cocina a fuego medio, removiendo constantemente, hasta que el líquido se absorba y el arroz luzca brillante.
Añade el calabacín rallado y el resto del caldo (400 ml) en dos tandas, cocinando 5 minutos por cada tanda, removiendo hasta que el arroz esté al dente y cremoso.
Mientras tanto, en una sartén aparte a fuego medio‑alto, calienta 1 cda de aceite de oliva.
Saltea las gambas (300 g) 2‑3 minutos, hasta que la carne se vuelva rosa opaco y alcance una temperatura interna visible de 71 °C (la carne ya no es translúcida).
Exprime el jugo de 1/2 limón sobre las gambas y sazona con sal y pimienta.
Cuando el risotto esté listo, incorpora las gambas y su jugo, mezcla suavemente.
Retira del fuego, añade el queso parmesano rallado (30 g) y la ralladura de la mitad del limón restante; mezcla hasta que el queso se derrita.
Sirve caliente, decorado con un chorrito de aceite de oliva y una pizca extra de pimienta.
tips: Remueve constantemente el risotto para liberar el almidón y obtener la textura cremosa.
Si el arroz aún está firme, añade un poco más de caldo caliente.

recipe.description: Calabacines asados, vaciados y rellenados con una mezcla de gambas, ajo y queso, ideal para una cena ligera.
instructions: Precalienta el horno a 200 °C.

recipe.title: Salade fraîche de haricots rouges, noix et fromage frais
recipe.description: Salade légère du soir, combinant haricots rouges, noix croquantes, fromage frais crémeux et parfum de coriandre et d'ail.
instructions: Égoutte les 2 boîtes d'haricots rouges, rince-les sous l'eau froide et réserve.
Hache grossièrement les 80 g de noix, puis fais-les torréfier à sec dans une poêle 3 minutes à feu moyen, jusqu'à ce qu'elles soient dorées et parfumées. Réserve en laissant refroidir.
Émince finement la gousse d'ail.
Cise la moitié de la botte de coriandre, sépare les feuilles des tiges.
Dans un grand saladier, mélange les haricots rouges, les noix grillées, le fromage frais émietté, l'ail émincé et la coriandre ciselée.
Prépare la vinaigrette : fouette 2 c. à soupe d'huile d'olive, 1 c. à café de vinaigre de cidre, le sel et le poivre.
Verse la vinaigrette sur la salade, mélange bien pour enrober tous les ingrédients.
Laisse reposer 2 minutes avant de servir pour que les saveurs se mêlent.
tips: Ajoute un zeste de citron pour plus de fraîcheur.
Cette salade se conserve 1 jour au frais, idéale pour un repas rapide le lendemain.
